SMTO-UI-0046 — Individual permission rules only work with Custom permissions

GUID: 9c6ad1ad-d182-4c19-8619-35adb0f1e506
Slug: ui-permission-custom-required
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • These permissions include rules for specific Skills, tools or commands, but the chosen setting is Ask, Allow or Deny, which can't hold such rules. Nothing was saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Permissions window, set the Permissions list to Custom if you want to keep your individual allow, ask or deny rules, then select Apply. Only Custom permissions can store rules for single Skills, tools or shell commands.
  2. If you wanted a simple preset instead (Ask, Allow or Deny), choose it from the Permissions list so the individual rules are dropped, then select Apply. A preset decides every case the same way, so it has to start with no individual rules.
  3. If the window keeps showing this message, select Cancel, open the Permissions window again and make your choice once more. Reopening the window reloads the saved permissions so you start from a clean copy.

What success looks like

  • Selecting Apply closes the Permissions window without an error, and the Permissions list shows the setting you chose.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep pressing Apply with the same choices; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A permission policy was rejected because it contains skill, tool or shell rules while its mode is not custom.

What this means

  • A permission policy includes individual rules while its mode is not custom. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • A permission policy includes individual rules while its mode is not custom.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect mode and nonempty rule families.

How to fix it

  • Non-custom modes (manual, full_access, deny) must have empty skill_rules, tool_rules and shell_rules; this is enforced by canonical() in agent_ui/permission_policy.js and AgentPermissionPolicy.canonical_rules in src/agent_runtime/permission_policy.py. Either set mode to "custom" (keeping default_confirmation_decision) or clear the rule lists before submitting the policy.
  • Choose Custom permissions to edit individual rules or remove those rules from the selected preset.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberate custom policy or a rule-free preset validates.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
